independence_statement: This review was produced independently. Reviewer 1 and Reviewer 2 outputs were not read.

paper.title: PaperToSkill: Turning Research Papers into Portable Agent Skills

review_scope_and_evidence_boundary.scope: Novelty, prior-work positioning, target-community impact, claim calibration, and the relationship between the original paper and the proposed EffectSlice direction.
review_scope_and_evidence_boundary.boundary: Novelty judgments are grounded in the manuscript, its rendered PDF, and the run-scoped literature table. The literature table is a structured local evidence pool rather than an exhaustive legal-priority or full-field search, so absence from it is not evidence of novelty. Several collision entries are abstract-level; exact subsumption should therefore be confirmed from full papers before making first-of-kind claims.
review_scope_and_evidence_boundary.pdf_visual_check: All nine rendered pages were inspected. The paper is legible, but pages 6-8 are dominated by sparsely placed tables, conclusion text, and fully pending external-evidence material; this dilutes the novelty narrative and visibly exposes submission incompleteness.

concise_verdict: The paper addresses an important practical problem and contributes a usable artifact pipeline, but its broad novelty claim is no longer defensible as written. Paper-to-agent and resource-to-skill compilation, compact grounded execution context, dependency-aware skill retrieval, cost-aware skill reduction, and skill-effect evaluation are already occupied by adjacent work. The only plausible original delta is a narrower deterministic, human-editable, source-span- and failure-boundary-aware note-to-SKILL.md compiler; the current experiments do not yet show that this delta yields independent fidelity or downstream impact. EffectSlice is a more promising and reviewer-defensible research question, but it is a separate-paper-scale pivot rather than an extension of the current manuscript.

manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.manuscript_claim: A paper-to-skill schema operationalizes research contributions as compact, human-editable skills.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.verified_novelty: Not verified as a broad schema contribution. Anything2Skill already compiles external knowledge into invocation conditions, action sequences, constraints, and outputs; SkillFoundry compiles heterogeneous scientific resources into executable, validated, composable workflows; Resource2Skill distills executable skills from multimodal resources. A paper note is a narrower input source, not by itself a novel computational object.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.defensible_delta: A deterministic and human-editable note-to-SKILL.md compiler that explicitly records line-span provenance, failure branches, inferred guidance, and transfer boundaries may be distinct, but the paper must demonstrate that this exact combination is absent from adjacent compilers and matters empirically.

manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.manuscript_claim: The deterministic extraction scaffold and source map form a reproducible conversion layer.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.verified_novelty: Potentially distinct as an engineering policy, but not yet a research novelty. Anything2Skill includes evidence-window support, SkillRAE targets grounded execution context, and Agent-Native Research Artifacts centers operational specifications and failure traces. The paper provides no direct comparison showing that deterministic line-span mapping improves correctness, editability, or trust relative to those mechanisms.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.defensible_delta: Claim deterministic traceability and conservative failure-boundary preservation, not first paper-to-skill conversion or first grounded skill compilation.

manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.manuscript_claim: A four-paper benchmark and deterministic/offline metrics establish structure, operational coverage, compactness, source grounding, and transfer readiness.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.verified_novelty: Not a competitive evaluation contribution in its present form. PaperBench and CORE-Bench offer execution-oriented reproduction benchmarks, while A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale targets marginal skill utility on roughly 500 skills. Four curated cases, author-defined rubrics, and offline readiness do not establish a new benchmark standard or a stronger evaluation methodology.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.defensible_delta: Present the tables as formative artifact diagnostics for this compiler, not as a benchmark or general skill-evaluation contribution.

manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.manuscript_claim: PaperToSkill differs from Paper2Agent because it produces portable natural-language skills with explicit source and failure boundaries and does not require an MCP server or runnable paper codebase.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.verified_novelty: The output-form distinction is real in the supplied evidence, but only at an artifact-description level. The manuscript does not run Paper2Agent, deploy an MCP server, compare setup burden, or show a fidelity/utility tradeoff. Paper2Agent already claims to turn papers and codebases into interactive reliable agents, so 'activating papers' is not available as novelty.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.defensible_delta: Position PaperToSkill as a lightweight, code-optional, inspectable artifact point in the design space, and empirically compare when that point is preferable to MCP packaging.

manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.manuscript_claim: PaperToSkill produces compact and portable execution context while preserving operational knowledge.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.verified_novelty: Compact grounded context and portability are crowded. ClawTrace attributes per-step cost and compiles preserve/prune/repair patches; Graph-of-Skills retrieves dependency-complete bundles under context budgets; SkillRAE compiles compact grounded execution context; SkCC targets cross-framework portable skill compilation. PaperToSkill does not present a new compression, dependency, or portability mechanism and cannot claim those objectives broadly.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.defensible_delta: Limit compactness to a measured property of the emitted artifact and portability to a hypothesis. Do not treat either as the novel mechanism without cross-framework or reducer comparisons.

manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.manuscript_claim: The eight-row real-reuse stress test contributes first downstream evidence for the approach.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.verified_novelty: The honest mixed-results artifact is useful, especially its patch-application and artifact-completion failures, but one run on eight heterogeneous rows is not a reusable empirical finding. AutoReproduce, PaperBench, CORE-Bench, and A Scientific Human-Agent Reproduction Pipeline already study executable paper reproduction at broader or deeper levels.
manuscript_claim_vs_verified_novelty.defensible_delta: Convert the observed failure modes into prospective compiler contracts and show on held-out tasks that those contracts reduce failures. The current table is exploratory evidence, not a standalone novelty claim.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Both transform static papers into agent-usable artifacts and aim to reduce manual method operationalization.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: Natural-language, human-editable SKILL.md; codebase optional; explicit source and failure boundaries instead of MCP server packaging.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: The delta is a design-point distinction, not verified novelty or impact, because the comparison never executes Paper2Agent.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Compiles heterogeneous scientific resources into reusable, executable, validated, and composable agent workflows.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: Single-paper curated-note input, deterministic text processing, line-span source maps, and human-editable output.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: This work makes the broad scientific-resource-to-skill contribution non-novel. PaperToSkill must prove that deterministic source/failure boundaries create a distinct benefit.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Compiles external declarative knowledge into reusable skills containing invocation conditions, action sequences, constraints, and outputs.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: Narrow paper-note domain and deterministic extraction rather than an LLM planner with taxonomy/confidence reconciliation.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: This is the closest conceptual subsumption of the claimed schema. Determinism is only a novelty if it yields measurably better traceability, stability, or editability.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Distills reusable executable skills from human-created resources, extending beyond text into multimodal tutorials.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: Paper-specific source spans and scientific-method failure/transfer boundaries.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: Further removes generic resource-to-skill compilation from the novelty set; PaperToSkill must claim a paper-specific audit contract, not the conversion category.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Compact skill construction, validation of preserve/prune/repair behavior, and cost-aware procedural analysis.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: PaperToSkill currently emits one compact artifact but does not trace or optimize per-step effect/cost.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: ClawTrace is a required baseline for any future claim that procedures can be removed while preserving benefit; it also motivates EffectSlice's narrower certificate layer.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Reducing loaded skill context while preserving dependency-complete execution bundles.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: PaperToSkill produces a standalone skill from a paper rather than retrieving bundles from a large skill graph.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: Original PaperToSkill should not claim a dependency-aware compactness mechanism. EffectSlice must submit Graph-of-Skills outputs to the same admission gate rather than compare graph machinery narratively.

comparative_positioning.overlap: Compiles compact, grounded, immediately usable context for downstream execution.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: Persistent, editable paper-derived artifact with explicit failure and transfer boundaries rather than retrieval-time context compilation.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: Grounded compact execution context is not novel. A direct matched test is required to show that persistent source-linked artifacts offer different value.

comparative_positioning.neighbor: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale
comparative_positioning.overlap: Evaluates whether skills causally improve task completion and exposes model/task-specific utility.
comparative_positioning.paper_to_skill_delta: Paper-specific artifacts and independently curated real-reuse tasks rather than task/rubric synthesis from arbitrary skills.
comparative_positioning.reviewer_judgment: PaperToSkill's four-paper deterministic rubrics and eight single-run rows cannot be positioned as a general skill-evaluation advance. The stronger opportunity is task-local, cost-adjusted eligibility and effect preservation, which EffectSlice targets.

strengths.strength: The paper identifies a real and timely usability gap between reading a method and operationalizing it for an agent.
The artifact-first scope is unusually honest: the paper explicitly does not claim arbitrary-PDF understanding and distinguishes curated-note conversion from end-to-end automation.
Source boundaries, inferred-guidance labels, validation checks, and failure branches are useful design choices for inspectable scientific agent artifacts.
The manuscript reports mixed and negative downstream rows rather than manufacturing an aggregate win, and follow-ups explicitly say when both conditions benefit.
The system and current eight tasks provide reusable infrastructure for a more specific causal question such as EffectSlice.

major_concerns.title: The related-work map omits the works that now define the contribution boundary
major_concerns.concern: The manuscript names Paper2Agent as the closest concurrent system, but the local 2026 evidence contains SkillFoundry, Anything2Skill, Resource2Skill, ClawTrace, Graph-of-Skills, SkillRAE, SkCC, Agent-Native Research Artifacts, and large-scale skill evaluation. These works cover most nouns in the current contribution statement: scientific resources, reusable skills, executable workflows, grounded context, compactness, portability, validation, and utility. Without direct positioning, reviewers cannot identify what is uniquely PaperToSkill.
major_concerns.concrete_fix: Rewrite Related Work around a comparison matrix with axes for input source, output artifact, code requirement, determinism, source entailment, failure-boundary representation, dependency handling, reducer behavior, task-local utility, and cross-framework portability. State which row/column combination is actually new and add executable baselines where outputs are comparable.

major_concerns.title: The six claimed contributions are a bundle of engineering artifacts rather than one load-bearing research innovation
major_concerns.concern: Schema, deterministic extraction, text-to-note scaffolding, a four-paper benchmark, local metrics, and a single-run stress test are listed side by side. None is developed into a mechanism or finding that would remain non-obvious after Anything2Skill and SkillFoundry. The paper needs one central claim, not six forms of project completion.
major_concerns.concrete_fix: Choose one of two papers: (A) an auditable deterministic note-to-skill compiler whose new claim is source/failure-boundary fidelity, or (B) EffectSlice's task-local effect-preservation certificate. Remove schema, benchmark size, and usage examples from the novelty list unless each supports that central claim.

major_concerns.title: Portable, grounded, and reusable are outcome claims, but the evidence is mainly self-defined artifact scoring
major_concerns.concern: The title and conclusion state portable agent skills, while the main real-reuse evidence is mixed, the real-reuse LLM ablation does not favor PaperToSkill, and the external cross-model and human-evaluation tables are entirely pending. The source-grounding claim is based on local span checks rather than independent semantic entailment. This gap materially reduces expected community impact.
major_concerns.concrete_fix: Until external evidence is complete, retitle around auditable note-to-skill compilation and change portability to a tested hypothesis. To retain the current title, complete repeated cross-model/cross-harness tasks and blinded multi-rater semantic/source validation with confidence intervals.

major_concerns.title: No strong adjacent-system baseline tests the claimed practical advantage
major_concerns.concern: Generic summary and abstract-only contexts are weak controls for a structured artifact. Paper2Agent is not executed, and the paper does not compare with Anything2Skill, SkillFoundry, ClawTrace, Graph-of-Skills, or SkillRAE. As a result, high deterministic coverage may reflect schema/evaluator alignment rather than a distinctive contribution.
major_concerns.concrete_fix: Add length-matched structured-summary, generic LLM proceduralization, expert-authored skill, and executable adjacent-system baselines. Score all outputs through an evaluator designed independently of PaperToSkill's schema and report both semantic fidelity and downstream task outcomes.

major_concerns.title: The target-community impact is asserted for ordinary users but not studied
major_concerns.concern: The motivation repeatedly invokes ordinary or non-expert users, yet there is no user study, editing-time measurement, comprehension test, trust calibration, or comparison of user success with paper, summary, and skill. Agent-facing contract scores cannot substitute for human utility.
major_concerns.concrete_fix: Either remove ordinary-user impact language or run a preregistered study measuring task completion, time, corrections, comprehension of use/failure boundaries, and calibration across paper, summary, and PaperToSkill conditions.

minor_concerns.concern: The term 'skill' is defined operationally but not positioned against the rapidly emerging lifecycle, compilation, retrieval, and cross-framework meanings of skill.
minor_concerns.fix: Add a compact taxonomy and state that PaperToSkill emits an instructional artifact rather than a learned policy, retrieval unit, executable tool server, or cross-framework IR.

minor_concerns.concern: The phrase 'reproducible conversion layer' is stronger than the demonstrated novelty and invites comparison with reproduction agents rather than artifact compilers.
minor_concerns.fix: Use 'deterministically auditable conversion pipeline' unless independent reproduction is shown.

minor_concerns.concern: The synthetic AI-Scientist-v2 result and retrieval-depth K=all observation are not integrated into the novelty argument and look like isolated project evidence.
minor_concerns.fix: Remove from the main narrative or connect it to a preregistered claim about context construction.

minor_concerns.concern: The rendered paper devotes an entire page to a future external-evidence diagram and completely pending tables while related work and method detail are compressed.
minor_concerns.fix: Remove pending tables from a review submission and spend the space on the novelty comparison, algorithm, and completed evidence.

minor_concerns.concern: The paper visually spans nine pages, with non-reference content continuing through page 8 and substantial unused whitespace on pages 6-7, creating an avoidable page-limit and presentation risk.
minor_concerns.fix: Resolve float placement and page-limit compliance before submission; this also forces prioritization of the central novelty story.

target_community_impact.potential_impact: High if the system can reliably turn papers into inspectable, editable, causally useful task artifacts with lower setup burden than executable paper agents.
target_community_impact.current_demonstrated_impact: Low to moderate. The current work demonstrates artifact generation and diagnostic infrastructure, but not broad user benefit, robust task success, or superiority to adjacent skill compilers.
target_community_impact.impact_bottleneck: The paper measures whether its artifacts contain expected fields more convincingly than whether those fields change user or agent decisions on held-out tasks.

effectslice_assessment.candidate: EffectSlice: Eligibility-Gated Certificates for Task-Local Procedural Effects
effectslice_assessment.defensible_novelty: The potentially defensible operation is not pruning. It is the reducer-agnostic admission decision that first requires a complete paper-derived artifact to have a sealed positive cost-adjusted effect on an independently locked user task, then certifies only a strict nonempty source-grounded subset whose effect, contracts, and guardrails remain equivalent under one preregistered confirmation family, while retaining all abstentions and baseline outputs in the decision rate.
effectslice_assessment.unresolved_novelty_risk: The run-scoped evidence itself flags ClawTrace as the almost-prior and leaves older behavior-preserving program reduction and statistical delta debugging insufficiently audited. A targeted full-text scoop check is required before first-of-kind language.
effectslice_assessment.reason: The original paper asks whether curated notes can be compiled into compact skill artifacts. EffectSlice asks whether an already beneficial complete artifact can be reduced while preserving an independently measured net task effect under a sealed statistical certificate. This changes the central hypothesis, output object, method, theory burden, baseline family, primary endpoint, and experimental campaign. PaperToSkill's source maps, artifacts, and eight tasks are reusable infrastructure, but the manuscript would need a new title, abstract, related work, method, experiments, and conclusions.
effectslice_assessment.recommended_relationship_to_original: Treat the current PaperToSkill paper as an infrastructure/artifact paper and EffectSlice as a follow-on methods paper. In the current manuscript, EffectSlice can appear only as future work or a preregistered direction, not as a late contribution used to rescue novelty.
minimum_evidence_for_effectslice: At least four genuinely new held-out paper-task pairs after freezing all development choices.
Matched direct ClawTrace, Graph-of-Skills, and SkillRAE outputs passed through the identical eligibility and sealed confirmation gate.
Correctly admitted nonempty compact-artifact rate, false-admission rate, cost, and abstention rate as declared endpoints.
M_tau-label permutation negative control on untouched confirmation seeds.
Targeted full-text comparison to behavior-preserving program reduction and statistical delta debugging.

concrete_revision_paths.goal: Salvage PaperToSkill as a narrow artifact/compiler paper.
actions: Retitle around auditable deterministic note-to-skill compilation; remove unqualified portable and reproducible language.
Define the single contribution as deterministic source/failure-boundary compilation and treat schema, tables, and examples as supporting artifacts.
Add the full 2025-2026 comparison set and an explicit mechanism-by-mechanism positioning table.
Run strong matched baselines and independent semantic/source evaluation.
Complete repeated real-reuse evidence or scope impact to artifact auditability.
Remove pending external tables and resolve page layout.

concrete_revision_paths.goal: Build a separate methods paper around task-local effect-preservation admission.
actions: Use PaperToSkill only as the artifact/source-map substrate.
Lead with positive-full-effect eligibility, abstaining certificate semantics, and the common sealed gate for reducer outputs.
Disclaim established reduction, graph, provenance, and statistical machinery.
Complete the held-out campaign and older-family novelty audit before manuscript integration.
Do not combine the original six contributions with EffectSlice; they answer different research questions.

novelty.rationale: A narrow deterministic traceability delta may exist, but the broad paper-to-skill and compact portable artifact claims collide with multiple adjacent systems.

positioning.rationale: The manuscript positions primarily against Paper2Agent and omits the most important recent skill compilers, reducers, retrieval systems, and evaluators.

significance_and_impact.rationale: The problem matters, but demonstrated impact is limited to four curated artifacts and mixed single-run reuse evidence.

claim_calibration.rationale: Results and limitations are unusually honest, but title, abstract, discussion, and conclusion retain stronger portable/reproducible language than the evidence supports.

overall.rationale: At the current revision, novelty positioning is incomplete and the only defensible delta is not validated against adjacent systems. Pending external evidence and the lack of a single load-bearing contribution amplify the novelty problem rather than merely reflecting missing polish.

confidence.rationale: High confidence in the manuscript-level judgment and overlap map; not maximum because the local literature table is not exhaustive and some newest neighbors are represented at abstract level.
